note: These are Jev's judgments, not measurements: for each key moment and industry, Jev (TypeSafe System One) placed how directly the moment changed the rules, costs, demand or competition the industry faced in the United States in the five years after it on the five levels below, judging from the moment's gated claim and its own knowledge of the period. `score` is the probability-weighted level (0-4), `confidence` how concentrated the probabilities are (1 all on one level, 0 an even spread or worse), `p` the probability of each level, 0 to 4. Built by Tools/politics/touches.py; Tools/politics/build.py merges the industries scored 1 or more into politics.json.
state: `moment` holds the key moment's title, its date as the research gives it, its kind (law, regulation, trade, monetary, treaty or conflict) and the claim of its gate-verified fact (Docs/research/politics/key-moments.json); `industries` the 25 industries of Assets/Resources/Data/economy/industries.json by id, each with its name, its tier's name, its NAICS coverage and its blurb (as `description`). Nothing else.
instructions: `moment` is a key moment for the economy of the United States (a law, a regulation, a trade action, a monetary turn, a treaty or a conflict), and `industries` lists the industries of the US economy, each with its name, tier, NAICS coverage and description. How directly did `moment` change the rules, costs, demand or competition that the {name} industry (`industries.{id}`) faced in the United States in the five years after `moment.date`? Judge from `moment.claim` and well-established knowledge of the moment and of those five years; leave out anything after those five years unless `moment.claim` states it. A measure that reached every industry through the economy as a whole, such as a broad tax cut, a change in the central bank's interest rates or the general demand of a war, counts for the {name} industry only as far as it bore on it more than on most industries.

levels.situation: Not at all, or only through the economy as a whole: in those five years the rules, costs, demand and competition of the {name} industry in the United States owed nothing in particular to the moment; whatever it felt of the moment, most industries felt alike.
levels.includes: an industry tied to the moment only by the buying and selling that link every industry to every other

levels.situation: Indirectly: the moment reached the {name} industry only at one remove, through the price of a minor input or through more or less business brought by a change in another industry, while its own rules, main costs and competition stayed as they were.
levels.excludes: a tie only through the buying and selling that link every industry to every other

levels.situation: A clear but secondary effect: the moment itself changed the rules, costs, demand or competition of the {name} industry in the United States, more than it changed most industries', though the industry was not among those the moment changed most.

A direct effect on a large part of the {name} industry: the industry was among those the moment changed most, in the rules, main costs, demand or competition that much of it faced in the United States.
levels.includes: a sharp change in the price or supply of what the industry mainly sells or of one of its main inputs

levels.situation: Written for, or aimed squarely at, the {name} industry: changing its rules, structure, costs or competition, or the supply of what it sells, was the moment's main purpose.

placeholders: {name} is the industry's name and {id} its id in `industries`, in the instructions and each level.
